rationale: Registered the successor execution for the last unexercised consequence: the harness adds a lost_entry_discard case on a five-voter committed configuration. The leader demotes all four peers (committed single-voter configuration), applies 100 commands, snapshots that configuration, promotes all four back to voters (committed five-voter configuration), then every instance is stopped. The former leader is restarted with the case's flag, acknowledges one uniquely named commit with the other four down, and is stopped again; the four voters are rebuilt with the flag disabled, a majority elects leadership without the payload, that leader is stopped so the remaining three elect once more in a strictly higher term, and only then is the holder rebuilt so the higher-term leadership must replicate over it. Construction-time local feedback: with the flag enabled the acknowledged payload was absent from every store after the holder rejoined (copies_after_rejoin 0, discarded true), while with the flag disabled nothing was acknowledged at all ("node is not the leader").

scope.description: Whether an acknowledged commit taken on a reconstructed smaller configuration survives once a majority of the committed configuration that never held it forms leadership. Fifteen in-process cases: the thirteen previously exercised restart shapes plus a lost_entry_discard case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a five-voter cluster is collapsed to one voter, snapshotted, made five voters again, stopped, and its former leader restarted, acknowledged on one copy, stopped; four voters return with the flag disabled, elect twice so the second leadership is in a higher term, and only then is the holder rebuilt and every store scanned for the payload.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; rebuilt instances are reconnected to each other in both directions.
The committed configuration has five voters while the restarted holder's snapshot metadata carries the demoted single-voter configuration, so the reconstructed quorum is one of five.
The four returning voters are rebuilt with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled on purpose, so their own configuration comes from their logs and their leadership exercises the committed configuration.

The extra election is a legal sequence: after the first returning leader is stopped the remaining three of five still form a quorum, so they elect again in a strictly higher term before the holder rejoins; the payload is searched for in every store across each store's first to last index.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, crashes of the remaining majority, membership changes after the acknowledged commit, and any claim about how a client would learn of the loss beyond the completed Apply.

experiment.prefix: The new case builds a five-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 5, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), demotes all four non-leader peers, applies 100 commands, takes leader.Snapshot(), promotes all four back with their addresses and applies five more entries, reads the last configuration entry, its voter count, the snapshot metadata and the tracked commit index, and emits a discard_inputs CA_EVENT. It stops every instance, rebuilds the former leader over its own stores with the case flag, waits for leadership, applies one uniquely named payload recording whether the future completed and at which index, and stops it again. It then rebuilds the four voters with the flag disabled, waits for one of them to lead, stops that leader, waits for the remaining three to elect again in a higher term, and only then rebuilds the original holder with the flag disabled and waits. It finally scans every rebuilt instance's log store for the payload and emits an entry_discard CA_EVENT with the reconstructed voter count, the acknowledgement and its index, the holder's and both returning leadership terms, how many stores still hold the payload, whether the holder still holds it, the holder's last log index after the rejoin, and the derived durable_on_majority and discarded flags.
experiment.responsibility: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and the leader's commitment is built from that configuration, so the durability of a client acknowledgement is decided by the reconstructed quorum rather than by the committed one.

comparisons.description: Five-voter case with the flag enabled: an acknowledged commit is expected to be durable on a majority of the committed configuration.
Five-voter case with the flag enabled: whether the acknowledged payload is absent from every store once the higher-term leadership has replicated over the holder.
Control: with the flag disabled the single running member of a five-voter committed configuration cannot acknowledge a commit at all.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds the five-voter lost_entry_discard case with its flag-disabled control, including the extra election that puts the returning majority in a strictly higher term than the stale holder's leadership so the holder's extra entries conflict and are truncated. Replaces the comparison set with the durability, discard and acknowledgement predicates.
